newsitem.title: SWEDEN: "Not now" view on EMU emerges in Sweden - minister.
newsitem.headline: "Not now" view on EMU emerges in Sweden - minister.

text.p: Health & Social Affairs Minister Margot Wallstrom has said there were indications that Sweden would take a "not now" approach to membership in Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU), daily Dagens Nyheter reported on Thursday.
"Much points to a 'not now'," Wallstrom was quoted as saying at a welfare seminar. "Many discussions around me also go in that direction."
Wallstrom said she herself was hesitant about EMU membership as it might threaten Swedish welfare policies.
"I have become irresolute about EMU as I'm not sure that it is possible to pursue Swedish welfare policies if we join," Wallstrom was quoted as saying.

Prime Minister Goran Persson has previously raised the issue about whether EMU will become a federal union -- removing power from member governments -- in which case Sweden would not be interested in participating.
The minority Social Democratic government will voice its opinion on EMU membership by the end of May, Persson said on Wednesday.
